summary:
Implemented the terminal window title feature in the repo; nothing committed and no tests, mypy, or Black were run, per instructions.

Changes:
- rich/segment.py: added SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16 after ERASE_IN_LINE; added Tuple[ControlType, str] to the ControlCode union.
- rich/control.py: added the SET_WINDOW_TITLE formatter emitting ESC ] 0 ; title BEL, and the Control.title(title) classmethod with an Args docstring.
- rich/console.py: added Console.set_window_title(title) -> bool beside show_cursor. It checks only is_terminal, writes Control.title through self.control, and returns True/False. Google-style docstring includes the restore/reset caveats.
- rich/_windows_renderer.py: one new elif branch in the legacy dispatch calling term.set_title(title). Win32 wrapper unchanged.
- CHANGELOG.md: Unreleased > Added bullet linking pull request 2200.
- tests/test_console.py: test_set_window_title (forced terminal, empty environ, skips on legacy_windows).
- tests/test_control.py: test_control_title (segment text, no style, control list).
- tests/test_windows_renderer.py: test_control_set_window_title (Windows-only, asserts set_title called once with "Hello, world!").

Unverified: tests and type checking were not run. Assumed the existing render path already drops control segments for non-terminal output, which I did not re-check.
